description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of mathematical problems across various educational levels and subject areas, categorized by difficulty and topic. The chart is composed of nine distinct slices, each representing a specific problem category with corresponding labels, percentages, and counts. The largest segment, in dark blue, represents Algebra – Olympiad-level problems, accounting for 21.19% (82 problems). The second largest is Algebra – High School, at 17.83% (69 problems), shown in light red. Pre-Calculus – High School follows with 14.21% (55 problems), depicted in brown. Combinatorics – Olympiad-level makes up 9.56% (37 problems) in green. Geometry – Olympiad-level contributes 6.46% (25 problems) in orange, while Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level also accounts for 6.46% (25 problems) in purple. Geometry – High School is 3.62% (14 problems) in light purple. Differential Equations – University-level is 3.62% (14 problems) in gray. Probability – University-level is 5.43% (21 problems) in teal, and Statistics – University-level is 4.39% (17 problems) in light blue. The slices are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top, and each slice is labeled with its category, percentage, and count, with lines connecting the labels to their respective segments. The chart does not include a legend, and the percentages are clearly displayed within or near each slice.
